t: A fire tender insured with IMT 13 (use confined to insured's own premises) is driven out on public roads to fight a fire at a neighbouring factory and is damaged. The claim is
o: payable, since use outside the premises for a mission to fight a fire is specifically excepted from the exclusion
payable at 66.67% because the discount of 33.33% was availed
not payable, as the vehicle left the insured's premises
e: IMT 13 excludes liability while the vehicle is used elsewhere than in the insured's premises, except where the vehicle is specifically required for a mission to fight a fire.

t: IMT 14 (use of vehicle confined to sites) is applicable to
o: private cars used inside gated residential colonies
all classes of vehicles including two wheelers
goods carrying vehicles used on sites to which the public have no general right of access and which are not required to be registered under the MV Act
e: GR 35 / IMT 14 applies to goods carrying vehicles confined to sites not open to the public and not requiring registration under the MV Act, with a 33 1/3% discount; IMT 13 is used for other classes.

t: Under IMT 16 (PA to unnamed passengers in a private car), compensation is payable only if the bodily injury results in death or disablement within
o: twelve calendar months of the occurrence
six calendar months of the occurrence
three calendar months of the occurrence
e: IMT 16 and IMT 18 (unnamed passengers / unnamed hirer and pillion) use a three calendar month period, whereas IMT 15 (named persons) and IMT 17 (paid drivers, cleaners, conductors) use six calendar months.

t: A passenger covered under IMT 15 is seriously injured while intoxicated and travelling in the insured car. Under the endorsement the compensation is
o: payable in full, as PA cover is not affected by intoxication
not payable, as accidents occurring while the person is under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs are excluded
e: The PA endorsements (IMT 15 to 18) exclude death or injury traceable to intentional self injury, suicide, physical defect or infirmity, or an accident happening while the person is under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs.

t: For a vehicle imported without customs duty (IMT 19), where a replacement part is not available in India and no local catalogue exists, the insurer's liability for the part is limited to
o: the actual air-freighted landed cost of the part
nil, as imported parts are excluded
the manufacturer's works price plus reasonable cost of transport (other than by air) and the relative import duty, less depreciation
the IDV of the vehicle proportionate to the part
e: IMT 19 limits liability to the catalogue price in the country of repair less depreciation, or where no such list exists, the manufacturer's works price plus reasonable transport cost otherwise than by air plus import duty, less depreciation, together with reasonable fitting cost.

t: A private car owner opts under GR 39 to restrict TPPD cover to the statutory limit of Rs 6,000. IMT 20 is attached and the TP premium is reduced by
e: IMT 20 reductions: Rs 50 for two wheelers, Rs 100 for private cars, Rs 150 for three wheelers and taxis, and Rs 200 for other commercial vehicles. The option is available only at inception.

t: For premium computation the minimum value (IDV) of a private car exceeding 1500 cc is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Minimum IDVs for private cars: not exceeding 1000 cc Rs 15,000; 1000-1500 cc Rs 20,000; exceeding 1500 cc Rs 30,000.

t: For the purpose of the compulsory deductible in IMT 21 and IMT 22, the expression 'event' means
o: each day on which damage occurs
an event or series of events arising out of one cause in connection with the vehicle insured
e: Both IMT 21 and IMT 22 define 'event' as an event or series of events arising out of one cause, so only one deductible applies to all damage from one cause.

t: A private car owner (car above 1500 cc) opts for a voluntary deductible of Rs 5,000. Under IMT 22A the amount to be inserted as borne by the insured for each event is
o: Rs 7,000, the aggregate of voluntary and compulsory deductibles
Rs 3,000, the voluntary deductible less the compulsory deductible
e: IMT 22A requires insertion of the aggregate of the voluntary deductible opted and the compulsory deductible under GR 40 (Rs 2,000 for cars above 1500 cc): Rs 5,000 + Rs 2,000 = Rs 7,000.

t: A truck insured with IMT 23 has its headlights and tyres stolen while parked, the vehicle itself being undamaged. Under IMT 23 the loss is
o: not covered, as theft of these items is excluded under any circumstances and cover applies only when the vehicle is damaged at the same time
covered after 50% depreciation and a further 50% deduction
covered in full as the add-on premium of 15% was paid
e: IMT 23 covers loss or damage (excluding theft under any circumstances) to lamps, tyres/tubes, mudguards, bonnet/side parts, bumpers, headlights and paintwork of damaged portion, provided the vehicle is also damaged at the same time.

t: A music system insured under IMT 24 stops working due to an internal electrical fault with no accident. The claim is
o: not payable, as loss caused by mechanical or electrical breakdown of the fitting is excluded
payable up to the IDV of the item
e: IMT 24 indemnifies loss or damage to declared electrical/electronic fittings by Section I perils but excludes mechanical or electrical breakdown; liability is limited to the IDV of the item.

t: A car bought for Rs 10.50 lakh was insured for an IDV of Rs 10 lakh in the first year. At renewal after one year the ex-showroom price of the same model is Rs 12 lakh. Under GR 8 the IDV is computed as
o: last year's IDV of Rs 10 lakh carried forward
20% depreciation applied to the purchase price of Rs 10.50 lakh
15% depreciation applied to Rs 12 lakh, i.e. Rs 10.20 lakh
15% depreciation applied to last year's IDV of Rs 10 lakh
e: GR 8 bases IDV on the manufacturer's listed selling price of the model at the commencement of insurance/renewal, adjusted for depreciation; the 15% (6 months to 1 year) is applied to the current price, not to the previous IDV.

t: A taxi registered and operating at Lucknow falls under which rating zone?
o: Zone B for OD and Zone A for TP
e: For private cars, two wheelers and taxis there are only two zones: Zone A (Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai, New Delhi, Pune) and Zone B (rest of India). The three-zone scheme applies to other commercial vehicles.

t: A short period policy for 3 months is to be extended by a further 2 months at the insured's request. Under GR 12 the extension premium is charged
o: free of charge, as part of the original cover
at short period rates applicable to the extension
at the difference between annual and 3 month premium
e: GR 12 N.B.1 states that extension of short period covers or short period renewals, for any reason, can be granted only by charging premium at short period rates; such covers are not permitted for Liability Only policies.

t: Under GR 13, the own damage and liability components of premium in a package policy are to be rounded off
o: to the nearest rupee only on the total premium
to the nearest ten rupees, together
to the next higher rupee, together
e: GR 13 requires OD and liability components (and all loadings/discounts) to be displayed separately in the schedule, and each component to be rounded off to the nearest rupee separately.

t: The premium computed for a small pedestrian-controlled vehicle works out to Rs 68. Under GR 16 the premium to be charged is
o: Rs 100, the minimum premium per vehicle
e: GR 16 fixes a minimum premium of Rs 100 per vehicle; the lower minimum of Rs 25 applies only to vehicles specially designed or modified for the blind, handicapped and mentally challenged.

t: A two wheeler package policy is extended under IMT 31 for a rally. During the rally the deductible under Section I is
o: Rs 2,500 or the IMT 22 deductible, whichever is higher
nil, as the rally premium replaces the deductible
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). IMT 31 inserts Rs 5,000 for private cars and Rs 2,500 for two wheelers; for the duration of the event the Section I deductible is this amount or the IMT 22 amount, whichever is higher. Organised racing, pace making and speed testing remain excluded.

t: Under GR 23 a Certificate of Insurance for a motor vehicle is to be issued only in
o: the insurer's own format approved by IRDAI
Form 51 in terms of Rule 141 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules 1989
Form 52 in terms of Rule 142 of CMVR
e: GR 23: the certificate of insurance is issued in Form 51 under Rule 141 CMVR; the cover note (GR 22) is in Form 52 under Rule 142 and is valid for 60 days.

t: An insured with 35% NCB on his car dies, and his son inherits the vehicle. On renewal in the son's name the NCB
o: is allowed only if the son was a named driver
is restricted to the first slab of 20%
lapses, since NCB follows the fortune of the original insured only
can be passed on to the legal heir who inherits the vehicle
e: GR 27: NCB follows the fortune of the original insured, but on death of the insured it can be passed on to the legal heir who inherits the vehicle.

t: Towing charges payable under a Motor Trade Road Risks (Class F) policy are limited to
e: Towing limits: Rs 300 for two wheelers, Rs 1,500 for cars and commercial vehicles, Rs 150 under Motor Trade Road Risk, and nil under Internal Risks policies.

t: How many perils are covered under Section I of a Motor Trade Internal Risks (Class G) policy?
o: Ten, as in the standard commercial vehicle policy
Four - fire, theft, riot and earthquake
e: Class G covers loss or damage occurring in the insured's premises caused by accidental external and visible means only, whereas Classes E and F follow the 10 perils of the standard commercial vehicle policy.

t: Under a Class F (Road Risks) policy the standard geographical radius for used (registered) vehicles in the dealer's custody is
e: For new vehicles and chassis the normal radius is 80 km (extendable to 120 km at 15% extra); for used vehicles it is 160 km, extendable to 320 km at 25% and beyond 320 km at 50% of the difference between package and liability premiums.

t: Under Rule 43 of CMVR a dealer must maintain the register of trade certificates in Form 19
o: in duplicate, with the duplicate copy carried in the vehicle
in triplicate, one copy filed with the RTO monthly
in single copy kept at the showroom
electronically on the VAHAN portal only
e: Rule 43 requires the dealer to maintain the Form 19 register in duplicate and to carry the duplicate copy in the vehicle using the trade certificate.

t: The minimum value for premium computation of a pedestrian-controlled agricultural tractor not exceeding 6 HP is
e: Class D vehicles have a minimum IDV of Rs 50,000, except pedestrian-controlled agricultural tractors not exceeding 6 HP for which it is Rs 10,000.

t: A tanker carrying hazardous goods must, apart from the driver's hazardous goods endorsement, be fitted with
o: a GPS tracker approved by ARAI
a speed governor set at 40 km/h
e: Vehicles carrying hazardous goods must be fitted with a spark arrestor; the responsibilities of consignor, owner and driver are fixed, and the driver needs an endorsement after a 3-day recognised course.

t: A quadricycle is a vehicle category defined by
o: the number of seats, which must exceed six
limitations in weight, engine power and speed
e: The quadricycle is a European Union category for four-wheeled microcars designed to less stringent requirements and defined by limits on weight, engine power and speed.

t: A surveyor appointed on an OD claim is expected to submit his report within
o: 7 days from the date of appointment, failing which a status report with reasons for delay
e: The surveyor must submit the report within 7 days of appointment; in case of delay a status report with valid reasons is required, and repeated delay by a surveyor is reported to the Regional Office.

t: In addition to the 25% OD discount, a certified vintage car is allowed a discount on TP premium of
o: 50%, as directed by IRDA with effect from 1.4.2018
nil - TP premium is never discounted
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). GR 29 gives 25% discount on OD premium to vintage cars certified by the Vintage and Classic Car Club of India; a 50% discount on TP premium was additionally allowed from 1.4.2018.

t: A car with IDV Rs 4,00,000 has an assessed loss of Rs 2,80,000. The claim should be settled
o: on total loss basis by paying the IDV
on repair basis, subject to production of bills, as the loss does not exceed 75% of IDV
on cash loss basis after deducting 25%
e: Where the assessed loss does not exceed 75% of IDV (here 70%) the claim is a partial loss settled on repair basis against bills/vouchers (reimbursement or cashless through tie-up dealers).

t: After a total loss settlement (other than theft), the Regional Transport Office is informed by
e: After finalisation of a total loss claim the damaged vehicle is taken into possession, salvage disposed of per guidelines, and the RTO is informed by Registered A/D post.

t: A stolen car is recovered intact by the police two months after the insurer paid the total loss claim. The insured
o: has the option to repay the claim amount already paid and retain the vehicle
keeps both the vehicle and the claim amount
must hand the vehicle to the insurer without any option
must pay the insurer the current market value of the car
e: If the vehicle is recovered before or after final payment, the insured has the option to repay the claim amount already paid and retain the vehicle; police and registration authorities are also to be notified of the settlement.

t: In a dealer tie-up (cashless) claim, liability is confirmed to the dealer by
o: the surveyor, after verifying the vehicle records
e: Tie-up claim flow: dealer intimates and prepares the estimate, survey is appointed online, the surveyor verifies vehicle records and confirms liability to the dealer, after which bills/satisfaction note lead to approval and NEFT payment to the dealer.

t: The minimum value for premium computation of a motorised two wheeler of 200 cc is
e: Two wheeler minimum IDVs: not exceeding 150 cc Rs 5,000; exceeding 150 cc but not exceeding 350 cc Rs 6,000; exceeding 350 cc Rs 7,000.

t: A motorised three wheeler of 600 cc used for private purposes is to be rated as
o: a commercial three wheeler under Class C-1
a private car with 50% discount on OD premium, but not less than the two wheeler premium for the same cc
a two wheeler with side car
e: Motorised three wheelers used for private purposes are rated under Private Car; those below 750 cc get a 50% discount on OD premium subject to the premium not being less than that of a two wheeler of the same cc.

t: Under GR 36B the premium for optional PA cover to paid drivers/cleaners/conductors of a commercial vehicle (IMT 17) is, per Rs 10,000 of CSI,
e: GR 36B rates per Rs 10,000 CSI or part thereof: private car Rs 5, motorised two wheeler Rs 7, commercial vehicle Rs 6; the same scale (100%/100%/50%/100%) applies.

t: Towing charges from the place of accident to the workshop under a two wheeler package policy are payable up to
e: Standard towing limits are Rs 300 for scooters/motorcycles and Rs 1,500 for cars and commercial vehicles; higher limits can be bought under GR 47.

t: A private car (1600 cc) aged 4 years 3 months, IDV Rs 4,50,000, has its windscreen broken. Assessment before depreciation: windscreen glass Rs 18,000, rubber beading Rs 1,500, metal fender Rs 12,000, labour Rs 5,000. The amount payable is
e: Glass nil depreciation Rs 18,000; rubber 50% = Rs 750; metal 35% (4-5 years) = Rs 7,800; labour Rs 5,000; total Rs 31,550 less deductible Rs 2,000 (car above 1500 cc) = Rs 29,550.

t: Under IRDAI's 2024 norms, a surveyor must be appointed within what time of a claim intimation?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Appointment within 24 hours; survey report within 15 days; insurer's decision within 7 days of the report.

t: A 45-seater bus with IDV Rs 30 lakh is damaged; assessed repair cost after depreciation is Rs 24 lakh. Salvage value is Rs 4,00,000. The claim payable is
e: Rs 24 lakh is 80% of IDV, so total loss. IDV Rs 30,00,000 less salvage Rs 4,00,000 less compulsory deductible Rs 1,500 (passenger vehicle exceeding 36 seats) = Rs 25,98,500.

t: A 20,000 kg GVW truck aged 7 years, without IMT 23, is damaged. Assessment before depreciation: metal parts Rs 1,50,000, fibre glass parts Rs 20,000, plastic interior parts Rs 30,000, tyres Rs 24,000. The insurer's liability is
e: Tyres are excluded under IMT 21 (no IMT 23). Metal 40% (5-10 years) = Rs 90,000; fibre glass 30% = Rs 14,000; plastic 50% = Rs 15,000; total Rs 1,19,000 less deductible Rs 1,500 (GVW above 16,500 kg) = Rs 1,17,500.

t: A new car with a listed selling price of Rs 12,00,000 is 5 months old at the time of insurance. Its IDV under GR 8 is
e: GR 8 schedule: not exceeding 6 months - 5% depreciation; Rs 12,00,000 x 95% = Rs 11,40,000.

t: An insured enjoying 45% NCB lodges an OD claim during the year. Next year the OD premium before NCB is Rs 16,000. The OD premium payable at renewal is
e: A claim made or pending in the preceding year reduces the NCB to nil at the next renewal; the full OD premium of Rs 16,000 is payable.

t: An insured cancels his private car policy (annual premium Rs 9,000, no claim) exactly 5 months after inception. The refund under GR 24 is
e: Cancellation by the insured attracts short period retention: exceeding 4 months but not exceeding 5 months = 60% retained (Rs 5,400); refund = Rs 9,000 - Rs 5,400 = Rs 3,600.

t: For health insurance, the maximum time an insurer may take to decide a cashless authorisation request under the 2024 master circular is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Cashless authorisation within 1 hour of request; final discharge authorisation within 3 hours.

t: A commercial vehicle has a Liability Only premium of Rs 3,200 and an appropriate OD premium of Rs 8,000. The insured wants Liability plus Theft Only cover under GR 45B. The premium is
e: GR 45B: Liability + Fire only = liability premium + 25% of OD premium; + Theft only = +30%; + Fire and Theft = +50%. Rs 3,200 + 30% of Rs 8,000 (Rs 2,400) = Rs 5,600 (IMT 27).

t: A motor dealer's premises of 1,800 sq m with annual wages of Rs 20,00,000 is to be covered under a Class G Internal Risks package policy. The premium is
e: Class G package premium for area not exceeding 2000 sq m = 0.28% on wages + Rs 150 = Rs 5,600 + Rs 150 = Rs 5,750 (liability only would be 0.28% on wages alone).

t: A private car package policy is extended under IMT 31 for a rally lasting 4 days. The additional premium is
e: Rally extension for private car package policies: Rs 60 for the first day and Rs 30 for each succeeding day: 60 + 3 x 30 = Rs 150 (liability only policies: Rs 25 and Rs 15).

t: A private car owner opts for PA cover to 4 unnamed passengers (IMT 16) with a CSI of Rs 2,00,000 each. The additional premium is
e: GR 36B: Rs 5 per Rs 10,000 CSI for private cars = Rs 100 per passenger for Rs 2 lakh; for 4 passengers = Rs 400.

t: A motorcycle with a side car attached has a tariff OD premium of Rs 1,200. The net OD premium after the side car discount is
e: The two wheeler tariff allows a 25% discount on OD premium where a side car is attached: Rs 1,200 - Rs 300 = Rs 900.

t: A taxi owner opts for additional towing charges of Rs 2,500 under GR 47. The additional premium is
e: GR 47 for taxis: additional towing up to Rs 1,500 at 5%, and Rs 1,500 to Rs 3,000 at 7.5% of the amount opted; 7.5% of Rs 2,500 = Rs 187.50, rounded to Rs 188.
